tests.Scenario: Metrics at deployable thresholds on untouched hold-out
tests.Expected: Top-20% rule has lift ≥ 1.5 over prevalence (C3)
tests.Actual: Lift 1.42x (precision 0.167 vs prevalence 0.117); 0.5 threshold flags 0 patients; F1-optimal threshold flags 985 of 1000
tests.Issue: At 0.5 the model never flags anyone; the F1-optimal threshold flags nearly everyone — the model has no useful operating point
tests.Collaborating_Track: Data Science

tests.Expected: Calibration slope within 0.8–1.2 (C5) and Brier below baseline
tests.Actual: Slope 0.18 (95% CI -0.06–0.41); Brier 0.1043 vs baseline 0.1035
tests.Issue: Predicted risks are not informative about actual risk (slope far below 1; Brier no better than baseline)
tests.Collaborating_Track: Data Science

tests.Scenario: Error analysis: FN vs TP and FP vs TN profiles; do flags enrich for admissions?
tests.Expected: Errors show outcome-related, correctable patterns, and flagged patients are admitted more often than unflagged
tests.Actual: Flagged patients are admitted at 12.7% vs 11.5% unflagged (p = 0.31); 78% of admissions missed, 87% of flags false alarms. Profile differences (9 of 16 and 13 of 16 variables after Holm) mirror the features the score is built from (selection effect), led by DepartmentName/DayOfWeek/ProvinceName - categories with no demonstrated link to admission
tests.Issue: Flags are driven by noise categories, not by outcome-related patterns; there is no error pattern that feature fixes could remove
tests.Collaborating_Track: Data Science

tests.Scenario: Performance across segments (gender, age band, province, department, visit type, severity, chronic status)
tests.Expected: AUC consistently > 0.5 across segments; no segment where the model fails
tests.Actual: 34 segments: AUC 0.37–0.59; 3 intervals above and 1 below 0.5 (≈1.7 expected by chance); 0 significant after Holm correction
tests.Issue: No segment where the model works reliably once multiple testing is accounted for; results scatter around 0.5
tests.Collaborating_Track: Data Science

tests.Scenario: Overfitting: train vs CV AUC; learning curve
tests.Expected: Small train–CV gap and CV AUC rising with more data
tests.Actual: Candidate gap 0.081 (train 0.601, CV 0.520); learning-curve train AUC falls 0.78→0.61 while CV stays ~0.5; unconstrained forest train 1.000 vs CV 0.499
tests.Issue: Mild overfitting (train above CV) and no learning: CV AUC stays at ~0.5 as data grows while training AUC falls — the model fits noise. Flexible models only memorise it
tests.Collaborating_Track: Data Science

w01_stability.title: Stability of the candidate model
w01_stability.interp: Across 30 random splits the AUC averages 0.495 (sd 0.021, range 0.461–0.549); 40% of splits land above 0.50 — about what chance alone would give. On genuinely future data (Oct–Dec) the AUC is 0.480 with a 95% interval of 0.43–0.53. The Week 6 hold-out value (0.529) is one ordinary draw from this spread, not evidence of skill.

w02_roc_gains.title: ROC and cumulative-gains curves, hold-out set
w02_roc_gains.interp: The candidate's ROC curve hugs the diagonal (AUC 0.529; the interval 0.47–0.59 includes 0.50) and the gains curve is indistinguishable from random ordering. Flagging the top 20% captures 26% of admissions with precision 16.7% (lift 1.42x; random gives 15.5%). The model gives no practical advantage over choosing patients at random.

w03_calibration.title: Calibration of the candidate model
w03_calibration.interp: Observed admission rates in the ten risk groups stay close to the overall 11.7% regardless of the predicted risk, so the reliability curve is flat rather than following the diagonal (calibration slope 0.18, 95% CI -0.06–0.41, ideal 1.0). Predictions span only 0.03–0.35. The Brier score (0.1043) is no better than always predicting the average (0.1035).

w04_segments.title: Model performance by segment
w04_segments.interp: Across 34 segments the AUC ranges from 0.37 to 0.59 and almost every interval crosses 0.50. 3 interval(s) sit wholly above 0.50 and 1 wholly below (about 1.7 expected by chance with this many tests), and 0 segment(s) remain significant after Holm correction. Even the best segments (AUC ≤ 0.59) are far below the 0.65 criterion, so there is no segment in which the model can be trusted.

w05_overfitting.title: Overfitting and learning-curve check
w05_overfitting.interp: The candidate overfits mildly (train 0.60 vs CV 0.52): as data grows its training AUC falls from 0.78 to 0.61 while cross-validated AUC stays at ~0.5 — it is fitting noise, not signal. A deliberately unconstrained forest reaches a training AUC of 1.00 yet cross-validates at 0.50, the signature of memorised noise. More data of the same kind would not help.

w06_importance_power.title: Feature importance and planted-signal power check
w06_importance_power.interp: No feature is reliably useful: the largest mean importance is 0.0051 AUC points and 1 of 18 features are positive in every fold (≈0.6 expected by luck). Right: when a genuine Age effect is planted, the same pipeline recovers it (detected from a true AUC of about 0.57 upward) and the shuffled-label control averages 0.501. So the 'no signal' verdict reflects the data, not a weak test.

w07_refinement.title: Before/after: candidate vs refinements
w07_refinement.interp: All variants sit between 0.475 and 0.517 AUC — indistinguishable from the 0.50 baseline. The best refinement (R1 Clinical-core features) changes AUC by +0.019 (corrected-t p = 0.13), well short of the +0.02 needed, and on the untouched hold-out it scores 0.537 (95% CI 0.48–0.59) versus 0.529 for the candidate. Refinement changed behaviour but did not create skill: the information is not in the data.

w08_interface_tests.title: Scoring-interface tests, before and after refinement
w08_interface_tests.interp: Of 18 interface tests, the Week 6 scoring behaviour (V1) passed 8 and failed 10: it scored impossible values (Age = -5, Province = Mars), silently accepted a missing ChronicCondition (the CSV 'None' pitfall) and unreported extra columns, and returned a bare array. After adding a validated input contract and a documented output schema (V2), 18 of 18 pass. This is a genuine Test → Finding → Action → Retest cycle for the Data Science → ML Engineering hand-off.
